conventions.convention: Regular functionals are finite symmetric complex smooth compact coefficient families on X = R^d, evaluated on all real smooth fields. Homogeneous coefficients have no 1/n! normalization. Compact complex integrals are componentwise Riemann integrals, and pairings use no conjugation.

η is a formal parameter fixed by conjugation. The k-fold Wick contraction uses k independent pairs of variables and coefficient η^k/k!, without multiplying distributions at coincident points. W need not be symmetric; the involution assertion additionally requires Hermiticity.

The kernel change K is symmetric, and α_K = exp((η/2)Γ_K) intertwines the W product with the W+K product. The assertion is an algebra isomorphism; preservation of complex conjugation is not asserted for arbitrary complex K.

Time ordering uses the scalar supplier's (-+++) metric and H_μ without an extra prefactor i. Relative distributions are lifted by pairing K with z ↦ ∫Ψ(y+z,y)dy. Functional support is the union of coefficient-kernel coordinate projections. A ≽out B means every x−y avoids the closed past cone, including its boundary and zero.
S_z^H(V) is a formal series in z with coefficient ring P_reg[η,η⁻¹] and nth term (iz/η)^n T_n^H(V,…,V)/n!. It asserts neither coupling convergence nor an extension to singular local functionals.

Bounded Dyson evolution assumes Countable Choice, a compact interval possibly reduced to one point, strongly continuous self-adjoint bounded V, and a finite uniform operator bound. Integrals are strong vector-valued Riemann integrals with reversed orientation for t<s. Unitarity is asserted for real z; the later separated generator appears on the left.
The diagonal delta is on R^4×R^4 and pairs with Ψ by ∫Ψ(x,x)d^4x. The local quartic obstruction requires a nonzero real test g; g=0 gives a regular zero functional.

load_bearing.statement: An element of P_reg(X) is a finite symmetric coefficient family f₀∈C, f_n∈D_sym(X^n), evaluated by F_f(φ)=f₀+Σ∫f_n(x₁,…,x_n)∏φ(x_j)dx. Its kth derivative kernel is the finite sum with factor n!/(n−k)!, and higher derivatives vanish above the degree.

For d,n≥1, finite sums of elementary product tests are dense in D((R^d)^n), with approximants supported in one fixed compact product and every derivative converging uniformly. Symmetrized sums are dense in the symmetric subspace. If a finite symmetric-kernel polynomial vanishes on every real smooth field, every coefficient kernel vanishes.

For any continuous complex bidistribution W on X×X and regular polynomial F,G, the finite sum Ση^k⟨W^⊗k,F^(k)(φ)⊗G^(k)(φ)⟩/k! defines an element of P_reg(X)[η] and is associative. Hermitian W additionally gives (F⋆_W G)*=G*⋆_W F*.
T_n^H(F₁,…,F_n)=m_n exp(ηΣ_{i<j}D_H^{ij})∏F_i(φ_i), with T₀^H=1 and T₁^H(F)=F; each contraction lowers total degree by two. S_z^H(V)=Σ(iz/η)^n T_n^H(V,…,V)/n! is coefficientwise formal.

For X=R^4, ⟨δ_Δ,Ψ⟩=∫Ψ(x,x)d^4x defines a continuous complex-linear distribution with support exactly Δ={x=y}, symmetric under exchanging variables. No nonzero smooth function on X×X is supported on Δ.

Assuming the three named current scalar supplier interfaces, regular V,U with supports A,B satisfying A ≽out B obey S_z^H(V+U)=S_z^H(V)⋆_Wμ S_z^H(U) coefficientwise in z. Pairwise spacelike-separated supports give commuting regular star products and corresponding formal series.

concerns.concern: Steps 1.1 and 4.1 omit a short analytic justification needed to identify the scalar contraction with the field evaluation of its contracted coefficient kernel and then pass to tensor-test approximations. F3 supplies smoothness and parameter differentiation, but does not itself state continuity of the contraction operation in varying coefficient kernels or interchange with the batch's Riemann integrals. Its separate integral clause concerns Lebesgue integrals and assumes Countable Choice. On the fixed compact supports used here, finite-order distribution estimates give derivative-seminorm bounds for the contraction map; Riemann sums converge in those seminorms, justifying interchange and the density passage without that integral clause. These estimates should be stated or cited explicitly. The claim appears sound.

seams_checked.note: Opened qft-mf04 and its cited time-ordered-kernel item, together with the scalar shell/Fock definitions and smeared-scalar/causal-commutator interfaces. The consumer retains the (-+++) metric, H_μ without an extra i, positive-time Wightman ordering, symmetry, and spacelike agreement. It supplies its own relative-to-bidistribution lift and explicitly treats the scalar interfaces as draft conditional suppliers. The scalar supplier assumes Countable Choice; reliance on its exact interface includes that premise. The reverse check found no supplier assertion of a local Wick extension or convergent interacting construction that the consumer could inherit.
